page.description: Ready-to-use apps (compose stacks): pick a project, fill in the domain and deploy in one click. Once created, the stack can be changed like any compose app.

catalog.needProject: Create a project first: templates are deployed into a project.

directus.description: Headless CMS and data backend: a REST/GraphQL API on top of a SQL database, with PostgreSQL.

PUBLIC_URL.label: Public URL
PUBLIC_URL.hint: E.g. https://cms.example.com — must match the domain you attach.

ADMIN_EMAIL.label: Admin email
ADMIN_EMAIL.hint: The first admin account is created with this email.

excalidraw.description: Open source virtual whiteboard for sketches and diagrams. Static client, no live collaboration.

ghost.description: Publishing and newsletter platform, with MySQL 8.

GHOST_URL.label: Public URL
GHOST_URL.hint: Full site URL, e.g. https://blog.example.com — must match the domain you attach.

gitea.description: Lightweight Git hosting (issues, PRs, CI Actions), with PostgreSQL.

ROOT_URL.label: Public URL
ROOT_URL.hint: E.g. https://git.example.com — must match the domain you attach.

grafana.description: Dashboards and visualization for metrics, logs and data from many sources (data is kept in the built-in SQLite).

ROOT_URL.label: Public URL
ROOT_URL.hint: E.g. https://grafana.example.com — must match the domain you attach.

mattermost.description: Self-hosted team chat (a Slack alternative) with channels, threads and integrations, with PostgreSQL.

SITE_URL.label: Public URL
SITE_URL.hint: E.g. https://chat.example.com — must match the domain you attach.

metabase.description: Business intelligence: ask questions of your data and build dashboards without SQL, with PostgreSQL for its application data.

SITE_URL.label: Public URL
SITE_URL.hint: E.g. https://bi.example.com — used for links in emails and embeds.

ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY.label: Credential encryption key
ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY.hint: Encrypts the database credentials you connect. Do not change it once it is in use.

minio.description: S3-compatible object storage, suitable as a backup destination.

n8n.description: Workflow automation (a Zapier alternative), with PostgreSQL.

N8N_HOST.label: Public host
N8N_HOST.hint: Same as the domain you attach, e.g. n8n.example.com (used for webhook URLs).

nextcloud.description: Private file storage, sync and collaboration, with PostgreSQL, Redis (cache) and a separate cron service.

DOMAIN.label: Domain
DOMAIN.hint: E.g. cloud.example.com (without https://) — must match the domain you attach.

PROTOCOL.label: Public protocol
PROTOCOL.hint: https when the domain uses HTTPS; http only for local testing.

odoo.description: All-in-one ERP and business suite (CRM, sales, inventory, accounting, website), Community edition, with PostgreSQL.

MASTER_PASSWORD.label: Database master password
MASTER_PASSWORD.hint: Generated automatically. Needed to create, duplicate, back up or delete Odoo databases at /web/database/manager. After deploying, find it on the stack page: Settings tab, environment section, "Show values" button. Keep it safe.

umami.description: Simple, privacy-friendly web analytics (a Google Analytics alternative), with PostgreSQL.

uptime-kuma.description: Self-hosted uptime monitoring with status pages.

vaultwarden.description: Lightweight password manager compatible with Bitwarden clients (web, mobile, extensions).

DOMAIN.label: Public URL
DOMAIN.hint: E.g. https://vault.example.com — must be HTTPS for the web vault to work (except on localhost).

ADMIN_TOKEN.label: Token for the /admin page
ADMIN_TOKEN.hint: Generated automatically; needed to open /admin. Keep it safe.

SIGNUPS_ALLOWED.label: Allow sign-ups
SIGNUPS_ALLOWED.hint: Set it to false once your account exists; invite other members through /admin.

wordpress.description: The most popular CMS and blog platform, with MariaDB.

dialog.title: Deploy {name}
dialog.description: The stack is created as a compose app in the selected project and deployed right away.
dialog.name: Name

access.title: Access
access.description: Optional, can be set later in Settings. Domains are exposed through the proxy (point DNS to this server); host ports are exposed by IP, e.g. {example}.
access.proxyStopped: The proxy is not running (<path></path>); domains only become active once it is enabled.
